title: Box<dyn Error> in persona-grpc public library signature
description:
persona-grpc/src/server.rs:14-17:

    pub async fn serve(
        socket_path: &Path,
        service: WorkloadApiService,
    ) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>

rust.md: "No `Box<dyn Error>` in library API signatures. Use `thiserror` or a concrete error enum." persona-grpc is a library crate and this is its main entry point.

What goes wrong concretely: callers cannot match on the failure mode. personad/src/main.rs:64-68 has to do `return Err(anyhow::anyhow!("{e}"))` — it stringifies the error because there is nothing else it can do with it. It cannot distinguish "stale socket could not be removed" (io::Error, possibly recoverable by retrying as a different uid) from "address already in use" (another personad is running — should exit quietly) from "tonic transport failed" (bug). The error also loses `Send + Sync`, so it cannot cross a task boundary.

The function has exactly four failure sources: `fs::remove_file`, `fs::create_dir_all`, `UnixListener::bind`/`set_permissions`, and `tonic::transport::Error`. A four-variant `#[non_exhaustive]` thiserror enum covers it, and each io variant should carry the offending path as a structured field.

build.rs may keep `Box<dyn Error>` — that is a binary, not a library API.
close_reason:
Fixed in 5bb2259. ServeError is a #[non_exhaustive] thiserror enum with seven variants covering every failure serve() and bind_listener() can produce; each filesystem variant carries the offending path as a structured field. personad no longer stringifies -- it propagates with ? and keeps the source chain, which is possible because ServeError is Send + Sync (asserted at compile time by a test, so it cannot regress). Tests added for matchability, all mutation-verified: reporting the wrong uid, the wrong path, or collapsing the not-a-directory case into the generic variant each kill a test. Workspace clippy clean under -D warnings.

ONE PREMISE OF THE BEAD IS WRONG and was NOT implemented as written: it says a caller should distinguish 'address already in use (another personad is running -- should exit quietly)'. That case is unreachable. bind_listener unlinks any existing socket before binding, so a second personad takes the socket over and bind(2) succeeds; AddrInUse never surfaces. Recorded on the type rather than claimed as a distinguishable case, and the underlying problem -- a second daemon silently displacing a running one, re-homing every pseudonym because the two hold different ephemeral keys -- is filed as persona-5s4b.131.

The bead's variant count (four) was also low: prepare_socket_dir alone has three distinct failure meanings (not a directory, owned by another user, io), which were previously distinguishable only by message text.
